```{=html}
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The task</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Produce:</b> a one-page verification log for a model or a data analysis: each check with its result, one benchmark against a known case, one validation against measured data or an independent reference, and a rerun from a clean <span class="lx-term" data-term="clone">clone</span>.</li>
<li><b>From:</b> this page's battery study (the notebook has all five versions), or your own project.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> Trustworthy analysis reaches Proficient: reruns from a clean clone (or a complete audit trail); verification log; one validation against real data or an independent reference.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 35 minutes guided here, then about 2 hours on your own: the notebook, Git and your log.</p>
<!-- r5-study:start (written from the model by _tests/learn/test_r05-build-validate.js --write; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The study, its five buggy versions and the checks that catch them</p>
<p><b>How much would a 50 MW, 200 MWh battery have saved Prairie Town on Wednesday 20 August 2025?</b> One day of dispatch as a linear program; 50 MW, 200 MWh (4 hours) battery, 85% round trip; data: Wednesday 20 August 2025.</p>
<ul class="r5-static-rules"><li><b>Balance:</b> Plants + battery discharge − battery charge + unserved = demand, every hour. <span class="lx-hint">(24 rows)</span></li><li><b>Stored energy:</b> Stored now = stored an hour ago + 0.85 × charge − discharge (MWh). <span class="lx-hint">(24 rows)</span></li><li><b>Gas ramp:</b> The combined-cycle plant changes by at most 40 MW an hour, from 115 MW. <span class="lx-hint">(24 rows)</span></li><li><b>End of day:</b> The battery ends the day with the 100 MWh it started with. <span class="lx-hint">(1 row)</span></li><li><b>Sizes:</b> Each plant within its size and the weather; battery 0–50 MW, 0–200 MWh. <span class="lx-hint">(limits on the variables)</span></li></ul>
<ol class="r5-static">
<li><p><b>Version 1: a unit error.</b> Saving reported: <b>$12,150</b>. Most energy stored (the battery holds 200 MWh): <b>279.5 MWh</b>.</p><p>Caught by: <b>Units and sizes</b>. The battery holds more than its size: the energy limit was typed in kWh into a model that counts MWh.</p><p class="r5-static-code"><code>E = 200_000      # battery energy, from the spec sheet</code> → <code>E = 200          # battery energy, MWh (the sheet says 200,000 kWh)</code></p><p>Fixed: <b>$8,205.88</b>, and stored energy never passes 200 MWh.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Version 2: a sign flip.</b> Saving reported: <b>$19,058.82</b>. Hours charging and discharging at once: <b>22 of 24</b>. Net energy to the town, as the balance rows count it: <b>176.47 MWh</b>. Stored energy at the end of the day: <b>100 MWh, as at the start</b>.</p><p>Caught by: <b>Balance and signs</b>. Charging was counted as supply, so the battery fed the town while filling up: energy from nowhere.</p><p class="r5-static-code"><code>supply[t] += c[t] - d[t]   # battery</code> → <code>supply[t] += d[t] - c[t]   # battery: discharge feeds the town</code></p><p>Fixed: <b>$8,205.88</b>. The battery now charges when the gas plant has room and discharges in the hours the peaker would run.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Version 3: a free lunch.</b> Saving reported: <b>$18,205.88</b>. Stored energy, start and end of the day: <b>100 and 0 MWh</b>.</p><p>Caught by: <b>Closure over the day</b>. The 100 MWh the battery started with cost nothing in the model, and it sold them in the evening.</p><p class="r5-static-code"><code># (no rule for the end of the day)</code> → <code>m.add(e[23] == E0)   # end the day with what it started with</code></p><p>Fixed: <b>$8,205.88</b>. The gap, <b>$10,000</b>, is the starting 100 MWh at the peaker's $100/MWh.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Version 4: a missing rule.</b> Saving reported (the fixed study: $8,205.88): <b>$8,205.88</b>. Gas plant's biggest change in an hour, in this solution (limit 40): <b>55 MW</b>.</p><p>Caught by: <b>Paper against code</b>. The formulation has 24 ramp rows; the code has 0. Today the headline happens not to move.</p><p class="r5-static-code"><code># (the ramp rows were never written)</code> → <code>for t in T: m.add(-40 &lt;= cc[t] - cc_prev[t] &lt;= 40)   # gas ramp</code></p><p>On <b>3 September 2025 (lesson 0's day)</b> the same code says the day without a battery costs <b>$102,600</b> instead of <b>$104,000</b>, and that the battery saves <b>$0</b> instead of <b>$1,286.49</b>.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Version 5: a leaked future.</b> Saving reported: <b>$8,205.88</b>. Schedule planned on: <b>20 August itself</b>.</p><p>Caught by: <b>Information at decision time</b>. Planned the day before, the battery could not know 20 August's demand, wind and solar.</p><p class="r5-static-code"><code>plan = solve(day='2025-08-20')            # the day itself</code> → <code>plan = solve(day='2025-08-19')            # what was known the day before<br>result = run(day='2025-08-20', battery=plan)</code></p><p>Planned on the day before (a persistence forecast) and then followed: <b>$2,100</b>, 26% of the $8,205.88 that [[perfect-foresight|perfect foresight]] gives.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><b>Benchmark</b> (a made-up day: 220 MW in every hour except 330 MW from 12:00 to 17:00, no wind or solar): by hand, 200 MWh × ($100 − $40 ÷ 0.85) = $10,588.24.</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts r5-bench"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Version</th><th scope="col">Saving on the benchmark</th><th scope="col">Matches the hand answer?</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Fixed study</td><td class="n">$10,588.24</td><td>yes</td></tr><tr><td>Version 1 (unit)</td><td class="n">$13,235.29</td><td>no</td></tr><tr><td>Version 2 (sign)</td><td class="n">$21,044.12</td><td>no</td></tr><tr><td>Version 3 (free lunch)</td><td class="n">$15,294.12</td><td>no</td></tr><tr><td>Version 4 (missing rule)</td><td class="n">$10,588.24</td><td>yes</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p><b>Validation:</b> with the U.S. fleet's measured 82% round trip (EIA, 2019 data) instead of 85%, the perfect-foresight saving is $7,939.02 instead of $8,205.88.</p>
<p><b>Rerun from a clean clone:</b> it failed on a data file read from one laptop's desktop; a download script with a checksum, relative paths, a pinned environment and a tag fix it.</p>
<!-- r5-study:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you run each version with a real solver in your browser, pick the check that catches its bug, fix it and run it again, then copy your verification log.</p>
</div>
</div>
<p class="lx-datanote"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><span>Demand, wind and solar follow the real hourly shapes of 19 and 20 August and 3 September 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (<a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/">EIA-930</a>), scaled to Prairie Town as in lesson 0. Prairie Town, its plants, costs and battery are illustrative; the benchmark day is made up. The solver is <a href="https://ergo-code.github.io/HiGHS/">HiGHS</a> (open source), loaded on your first run (about 3.5 MB, once).</span></p>
<div class="lx-card lx-notebook r5-nb">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Practice on your own · notebook and Git, about 2 hours</p>
<p>The same study in <code>scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs")</code>, with all five versions behind a switch. You write each check as a function, add the benchmark as a test, put the folder under <span class="lx-term" data-term="version-control">version control</span> and rerun it from a fresh clone.</p>
<ol class="r5-nb-steps">
<li>Download the notebook; the data are inside it.</li>
<li>Run it in Google Colab (<em>File → Upload notebook</em>) or locally with Python 3, NumPy and SciPy 1.9 or later.</li>
<li>For the Git part, work locally: the notebook lists the commands, and K8 (Git and reproducible notebooks) shows them step by step.</li>
</ol>
<p class="r5-dl"><a class="lx-btn small" href="notebooks/r05-build-validate.ipynb" download>Notebook (.ipynb)</a> <a class="lx-btn small ghost" href="../assets/learn/data/r05-build-validate.json" download>Study data (JSON)</a></p>
</div>
<div id="r5-workflow" class="lx-xgrid r5-flow">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Verify, benchmark, validate, rerun</p>
<ol>
<li><b>Formulation on paper</b>, then <b>code and data</b>.</li>
<li><b>Verification checks</b>: units, sizes, balance and signs, closure, paper against code, information at decision time. If one fails, fix the code and run every check again.</li>
<li><b>Benchmark</b>: a case with a hand answer. If it does not match, fix the code.</li>
<li><b>Validation</b>: measured data or an independent reference. If the model is not close enough for the claim, revisit the assumptions or narrow the claim.</li>
<li><b>Rerun from a clean clone</b>, then <b>report with limits</b>.</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div id="r5-exemplars" class="lx-xgrid">

<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans weak"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Weak log · Developing</p><p>I checked the model and the results look reasonable [1]. The battery saves $8,205.88 on 20 August [2], so it would save about $3.0 million a year [3]. The model was validated [4]. The code is in a folder on my laptop [5].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> No check is named, so nobody can repeat it or see what it would have caught.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> This is the perfect-foresight saving, and the log does not say the plan knew the day in advance.</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> One hot day times 365 is not a year: on 3 September the same battery saves $1,286.49.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> Validated against what? A validation names its data and the result of the comparison.</li><li value="5"><b>Falls short:</b> Nobody else can rerun a folder on one laptop.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong log · Proficient</p><p>Checks, each with its result: stored energy within 0–200 MWh in every hour [1]; each hour balances, with the battery feeding the town only as its stored energy falls [2]; the day ends with the 100 MWh it started with [3]; 24 ramp rows in the code, as in the formulation [4]. Benchmark: a made-up two-level day, hand answer $10,588.24, model $10,588.24 [5]. Validation: with the U.S. fleet's measured 82% round trip, the saving is $7,939.02 instead of $8,205.88 [6]. Saving on 20 August 2025: $2,100 with a plan made the day before, $8,205.88 with perfect foresight [7]. Reruns from a clean clone at tag v1.0 with the pinned environment [8].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> A size check with its range: it would have caught version 1.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> A balance check that also tests the sign convention: it would have caught version 2.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> A closure check: it would have caught version 3.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> Paper against code: the only check here that catches version 4 on this day.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> A known case, worked by hand, matched to the cent.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> Validation against measured data, with the effect on the result.</li><li value="7"><b>Works:</b> Both numbers, each labelled with what the plan knew.</li><li value="8"><b>Works:</b> A tag and a pinned environment let anyone get the same numbers.</li></ol></div>
</div>
```

:::

```{=html}
<div id="r5-rubric" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- r5-rubric:start (written by the test's --write mode from the checklist and LX.Rubric's staticHTML; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-xcard"><p class="lx-eyebrow">A verification log in nine lines</p><ol class="r5-static-rules"><li><b>Units:</b> Every input in the model's units, with the unit written beside it.</li><li><b>Sizes:</b> Every result within its physical size and limits.</li><li><b>Balance and signs:</b> Each period balances; a store's energy falls when it feeds the system.</li><li><b>Closure:</b> The end state matches the start, or the difference is valued.</li><li><b>Paper against code:</b> Each rule's rows counted against the formulation.</li><li><b>Information:</b> Every input was known when the decision was made.</li><li><b>Benchmark:</b> One case with a hand answer, matched.</li><li><b>Validation:</b> One comparison with measured data or an independent reference, with its source.</li><li><b>Rerun:</b> A clean clone at a tagged commit, a pinned environment, the same numbers.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts lx-rb-static"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Competence</th><th scope="col">Developing</th><th scope="col">Proficient (the bar)</th><th scope="col">Strong</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Trustworthy analysis<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Your log names each check with its result, one benchmark with its hand answer, one validation with its data source, and the tag a clean clone reran.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Results cannot be rerun.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Reruns from a clean clone (or a complete audit trail); verification log; one validation against real data or an independent reference.</td><td data-l="Strong">Independent reproduction by someone else; validation on data not used to build the analysis.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<!-- r5-rubric:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="r5-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="optimal" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If the solver says optimal, the study is right.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. All five versions on this page solved to optimal. Optimal means the best answer to the equations as written, bugs included.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="bench" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A study that matches its benchmark has no bugs.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Version 4, with no ramp rows at all, matched the benchmark to the cent: <!-- r5-myth-bench:start -->$10,588.24<!-- r5-myth-bench:end -->. A benchmark tests only what it exercises.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="same" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Verification and validation are two words for the same check.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. <span class="lx-term" data-term="verification">Verification</span> compares the code with its own equations; <span class="lx-term" data-term="validation">validation</span> compares the equations with the real system, for the purpose of the claim.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="rerun" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “With the same data, code and pinned environment, a clean clone should reproduce the reported numbers.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact, for the reported numbers. When several plans cost exactly the same, another solver version may return a different plan at the same cost; report the cost, and the plan only where it is the only one.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>From Proficient to Strong: someone else reruns it, on data you did not use</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

The rubric's Strong level asks for two more things. First, independent reproduction: a colleague reruns your study from your repository, without your help, and reports any difference. Second, validation on data the analysis did not use to build itself: here, the same battery on other days of 2025 (3 September gives a very different saving), or a real battery's metered schedule. In the capstone research project you show both in the verification log.

Verification and validation for computer models have their own literature; for energy-system optimization studies, DeCarolis and co-authors set out good practice, including how to test a model and report what it leaves out ([DeCarolis et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2017.03.001)).

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Perfect foresight is a modelling choice, not a bug, as long as it is named</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Many planning studies schedule storage knowing the whole day, week or year in advance, because it is simple and gives an upper bound on what storage can earn. That is fine when the report says so. It becomes the leaked future of version 5 when the upper bound is reported as what an operator would have saved. Between the two sit rolling-horizon schedules that re-plan as forecasts improve (M5, upcoming in the Modeler tier).

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```
